topic.title: Historical feedback value beyond advertisement context
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and history policy, how much of the strongest joint model's click-AUC gain depends on observed historical actions, and does that dependence interact with task-conditioned history representation?
topic.hypothesis: Historical actions may contribute predictive information beyond advertisement and context content, with task conditioning determining its utility. Starting from the frozen joint best, compare action availability and task conditioning with factorial removal and matched-capacity replacement controls, preserving every original history-mask restriction and the training protocol. Retain the unchanged joint model, both source bests, context-only reference and shared baseline as utility controls; measure parameters, training and inference cost. A reproducible action-removal loss surviving replacement controls would support feedback utility; an interaction would support dependence on task conditioning. No loss, a capacity or optimization explanation, or failure to repeat would weaken that account. Neither source gains nor a single favorable contrast establish the mechanism.
